Note::TexAccessor::set_macro¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::set_macro(std::string_view name,
                               std::string_view body) const

Define One Cell-Local Control Word¶

set_macro() returns TeX source whose first declaration defines name with body. It is useful when every cell must carry a self-contained declaration before later expansion, rendering, storage, or transport. The method does not expand uses of the macro; macro_subs() performs that separate job. It also differs from cmd_sub(), which replaces occurrences lexically without creating a declaration.

Before inserting the declaration, the method removes every complete existing definition of the same name written with \newcommand, \renewcommand, \providecommand, or \def. Definitions of other names and ordinary uses are untouched. The canonical inserted spelling is \newcommand{\name}{body} followed by one newline and the remaining source. Consequently, applying the method again changes the definition rather than accumulating duplicates.

name may be written as unit or \unit. After the optional leading slash it must be a non-empty TeX control word containing letters or @; a starred name, spaces, punctuation, and multiple leading slashes reject. body is inserted literally and may contain nested groups and control words. The declaration is zero-argument, so an unescaped # parameter marker rejects; braces must also balance, with escaped braces ignored by the balance check. Both arguments are validated before the receiver is read.

The operation is out-of-place and cell-wise. It returns a Text Note with the receiver’s rank and shape, including scalar and empty cells. Undefined state propagates after argument validation; defined non-Text Notes reject. Processing is linear in source bytes and allocates one output string per cell.

Example 1: Replace Or Add A Definition¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\renewcommand*{\unit}{old}
value=\unit)",
    "plain source",
    R"(\newcommand{\unit}{cm}\unit + \unitless)"});
std::cout << source.tex().set_macro("unit", R"(\mathrm{kg})") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\newcommand{\\unit}{\\mathrm{kg}}\nvalue=\\unit", "\\newcommand{\\unit}{\\mathrm{kg}}\nplain source", "\\newcommand{\\unit}{\\mathrm{kg}}\n\\unit + \\unitless"]

The longer \unitless use is not mistaken for \unit; only declarations are removed, not uses.

Example 2: Both Name Spellings Are Equivalent¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note("value=\\unit");
const auto bare = source.tex().set_macro("unit", "m");
const auto slashed = source.tex().set_macro(R"(\unit)", "m");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "same=" << ((bare == slashed).all().bool_item()) << '\n';

Output¶

same=true

Example 3: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "", R"(\unit)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().set_macro("unit", "s") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["\\newcommand{\\unit}{s}\na", "\\newcommand{\\unit}{s}\nb"],
  ["\\newcommand{\\unit}{s}\n", "\\newcommand{\\unit}{s}\n\\unit"]
]

Example 4: Invalid Definitions Reject Before Receiver Access¶

for (const auto bad_body : {false, true}) {
  try {
    (void)(bad_body
        ? pluss::Note::undefined().tex().set_macro("unit", "{x")
        : pluss::Note::undefined().tex().set_macro("bad name", "x"));
  } catch (const pluss::Error&) {
    std::cout << (bad_body ? "unbalanced body" : "bad name")
              << ": rejected\n";
  }
}

Output¶

bad name: rejected
unbalanced body: rejected

Example 5: Undefined State And Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().set_macro("unit", "m").defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex()
      .set_macro("unit", "m");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

undefined=false
Int64: rejected
